newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat drops to new lows as SRW sales stymied.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat drops to new lows as SRW sales stymied.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower and new contract lows were set on disappointment about the sales pace for soft red winter wheat, traders said.

"There was no soft red winter business and even though prices are starting to get competitive, there's still a lot of wheat around the world and overall the values are cheap," said Skip Searcy wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.

Egypt over the weekend bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat, Pakistan is in the market for 200,000 tonnes of white wheat and Algeria Monday announced a snap tender for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat.
Last week Algeria bought wheat from Argentina and France.

"Wheat continues to react to the fact it is overvalued compared to world values," said Mark Cermak of Chicago trade house O'Connor and Co. "Argentina is selling wheat and that has the Europeans putting on subsidies."
After the close there was news Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies pegged Argentina's wheat exports this season to rise to 9.6 million tonnes from the 1995-96 level of 4.45 million tonnes.
Wheat closed unchanged to 7-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 7-1/2 at $3.82-1/4.
Also Monday, there was news USDA has stopped issuing export certificates for wheat shipments to Turkey which contributed to the persistent bearish slide in CBOT wheat futures.
The new contract low for March is $3.75 per bushel, down from the previous low of $3.78 set Friday.
Traders said funds continued to add to their short positions in the wheat pit.
"The commitments showed funds were short and I think that will get bigger," Searcy said of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders data released Friday.
The data showed non-commercials, including funds, were short nearly two to one as of October 22.

The CFTC report Friday showed as of October 22, non-commercials were short wheat 81.930 million bushels and long 42.485 million. Since October 8 the short tally increased 10.490 million bushels and longs increased 195,000 bushels.

The key moving averages showed wheat remains bearish but the short-term nine day relative strength index closed at 21.338 points. Technicians generally consider an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
First support in the December was at $3.83-1/2 and second support was at $3.72-3/4. First resistance was at $3.93-3/4 and second resistance at $4.04-1/4.
The session low for December was $3.80 and the session high was $3.90.

Key players included LFG Futures with three million bushels sold in the December, one-half million of that in late dealings, traders said. FIMAT Futures and LIT America each sold 1.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,000, down from 16,848 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Smith Barney sold 300 March $4.00 calls at eight cents and Merrill Lynch Futures bought 350 March $4.30 calls at 2-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000, down from 10,578 Friday.
